_meta.tagline: Collaborative map of gender-based violence cases in Latin America
_meta.description: Collaborative documentation of femicides and abuse in Latin America. Three verified moderators approve each case before it is published on the map.

hero.headline: Collaborative map of gender-based violence cases
hero.subheadline: Every case on this map was reviewed and approved by three independent moderators. If you know of a case with a verifiable public source, you can report it.

intro.title: What is Cuidado Amiga?
paragraphs: Cuidado Amiga is an open-source project that documents femicides, abuse, and harassment in Latin America. Cases are reported by anyone and approved by three verified moderators before being published on the map.
We do not sell or monetize any personal data. All published information comes from verified public sources: news articles, official reports, or records from recognized organizations.

comoFunciona.title: How does Cuidado Amiga work?
comoFunciona.subtitle: A collaborative map with independent verification. Here is how each case is processed.

sections.title: How does a case enter the map?
items: Anyone can report a case using the «+ Report a case» button.
The case enters pending state — it is not published automatically.
Three verified moderators review it independently.
To be approved, it needs at least one verifiable public source: a news article, an official report, or a record from a recognized organization.
If all three approve → it is published. If any one rejects → it is not published.
The published case always includes the link to the original source.

sections.title: What information is published?
items: Full name of the aggressor
Date of the event
Country and city
Type of case (femicide / abuse / harassment)
Photo (only if publicly available)
Link to the verified source

sections.title: What is NOT accepted?
items: Cases without a verifiable public source
Cases based solely on anonymous testimony without backing
Information about minors
Information that could put family members or witnesses at risk
Reports without a confirmed date

sections.title: Who are the moderators?
sections.body: Moderators are manually verified by the Cuidado Amiga team. Each one signs a code of conduct and works independently.

sections.title: Privacy and data
sections.body: We do not sell or monetize any personal data. All information published on the map comes from verified public sources. We do not store data from people reporting cases beyond what is necessary for the moderation process.

protocolo.title: Moderation protocol
protocolo.subtitle: This document defines the criteria and conduct that govern the work of Cuidado Amiga moderators. It must be read before requesting access.

sections.title: Criteria for publishing a case
items: It must have at least one verifiable public source: a news article, an official report, or a recognized organization.
Cases without a name or without a confirmed date are not published.
The photo must be public — not taken from private social networks.

sections.title: What is never published
items: Information about minors.
The exact address of the victim's home or family.
Information that could put family members or witnesses at risk.

sections.title: Moderator conduct
items: Confidentiality about the data they handle.
No sharing of screenshots from the administration panel.
Report any attempt at manipulation or external pressure.

sections.title: Causes for removal as a moderator
items: Publishing cases without full validation by 3 moderators.
Leaking sensitive information.
Prolonged inactivity without prior notice.

recursos.title: Where to report?
recursos.subtitle: Emergency lines, organizations, and official resources for gender-based violence victims in Latin America. If you are in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.

emergencyBanner.title: If you are in immediate danger
emergencyBanner.body: don't wait — call your country's emergency number (911 in most countries). Your safety comes first.

recursos.missingBanner: Know a resource that is missing? Write to {email} and we will add it.

items.a: Anyone can report a case, but no case is published automatically. It goes through review by three independent moderators before appearing on the map.

items.q: How do I know the information is true?
items.a: Each case requires at least one verifiable public source to be approved: a news article, an official report, or a record from a recognized organization. Without a source it is not published.

items.q: What happens if someone submits false information?
items.a: The triple-validation system is designed to prevent that. If a false case were published by mistake, anyone can report it to cuidadoamiga@proton.me and it will be removed immediately.

items.q: Can I report a case from my country even though the site is about Latin America?
items.a: Yes. The site documents cases from all Latin American and Caribbean countries.
You can report cases with verified sources, become a moderator through /unirse, or share the site with feminist organizations in your country.
